findings.claim: The independent Lyapunov route (positive definite P) agrees with the numpy eigenvalue route on every route-family plant

hypothesis: The PLSR matrix route (Lyapunov solve, then the sign of max eig of the decrease form beyond the resolution) agrees with independent references -- numpy eigenvalues and SciPy's Bartels-Stewart Lyapunov solvers; PLSR's scalar gate (NOT_CERTIFIED when x^T M x > res |x|^2) fires only where the exact x^T M x is positive and the matrix route finds max eig(M) > res, on margin-separated plants and on near-threshold forms alike, and where the two cross together (at the top eigenvector of a form whose max eig(M) is within rounding of res) only where max eig(M) exceeds res less the rounding of the two; and the scalar quadratic route (the sign of x^T M x at sampled states) cannot certify definiteness and misses thin positive cones.
input_data: 30 continuous plants n = 2..5 (PCG64 seed 111) with |spectral abscissa| > 0.05
Thin-cone plant A = diag(-0.5, 5e-7), P = I (decrease form diag(-1, 1e-6)) with 64 random unit states (seed 1111)

Scalar-gate samples: every route plant with P = I at its own state and seven more (seed 1112); each of T107's 90 window and 12 -res straddle forms (seeds 107, 1071) at the computed top eigenvector of its decrease matrix and three seeded states; each of T107's 12 forms straddling +res (seed 1072) at its computed top eigenvector, where the scalar gate and the eigenvalue route cross together
mathematical_model: Rayleigh: x^T M x <= max eig(M) |x|^2 for every x, with equality only on the top eigenvector, so sampled negativity never implies negative definiteness. An unstable A has v*(A + A^T)v = 2 Re(lambda)|v|^2 > 0 for an eigenvector v, so P = I can never certify it. If the resolution bounds the error of the computed x^T M x (|x^T E x| <= ||E||_2 |x|^2), then x^T M x > res |x|^2 in float64 implies an exactly positive x^T M x and, by Rayleigh, max eig(M) > res. At a top eigenvector of a form with max eig(M) within rounding of res the two decisions read the same crossing: the computed x^T M x / |x|^2 can exceed the computed max eig(M) by at most (gamma_2n n + n^3 u) max|M| (dot-product error and the documented eigensolver term, to first order in u), so there NOT_CERTIFIED implies a computed max eig(M) above res less that bound. For n = 1 the decrease form is 2 a p (continuous), so the verdict must follow sign(a) whenever 2|a|p exceeds the resolution.
numerical_result: Solver agreement: max relative difference 1.73e-14 over 15 continuous and 4.50e-16 over 15 discrete PLSR solves (scipy.linalg.solve_continuous_lyapunov@1.16.2; scipy.linalg.solve_discrete_lyapunov@1.16.2). solve_lyapunov: 0 disagreements with numpy stability over 50 plants, 20 refusals (20 of them numpy-unstable plants). Verdicts: 0 stable plants not certified with their own P, 0 unstable plants certified with P = I. Thin cone: 64/64 sampled scalar decreases negative; PLSR codes {'DECREASE_NOT_DEFINITE': 64}. Scalar plants: {'-1': 'CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN', '-1e-10': 'CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN', '-1e-300': 'CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN', '-4.94066e-324': 'CERTIFIED_WITH_MARGIN', '0': 'NUMERICAL_INCONCLUSIVE', '4.94066e-324': 'NOT_CERTIFIED', '1e-300': 'NOT_CERTIFIED', '1': 'NOT_CERTIFIED'}. Scalar gate over 808 samples: violations {'not_certified_without_exact_increase': 0, 'not_certified_without_eigen_route': 0, 'eigen_route_on_exactly_negative_definite_form': 0, 'certified_where_exact_x_M_x_positive': 0}; agreement shares (scalar vs exact sample sign, eigenvalue route vs exact class, scalar vs eigenvalue route) {'route family': {'scalar_vs_exact_sample_sign': 1.0, 'eigen_vs_exact_class': 1.0, 'scalar_vs_eigen': 0.5675}, 'near threshold': {'scalar_vs_exact_sample_sign': 0.9607843137254902, 'eigen_vs_exact_class': 0.8431372549019608, 'scalar_vs_eigen': 0.7794117647058824}}; NOT_CERTIFIED shares {'route family': 0.1475, 'near threshold': 0.07352941176470588}. Coincident crossing (12 samples at the top eigenvector of T107's forms straddling +res): both routes fired at 7, neither at 5, the scalar gate alone at 0 and the eigenvalue route alone at 0 (decided by rounding); the quotient exceeded max eig(M) by at most 0.046 of the rounding bound; violations {'not_certified_without_exact_increase': 0, 'excess_beyond_bound': 0, 'certified': 0}. Conclusion: the matrix routes agree with each other on margin-separated plants; the scalar gate is sound against exact x^T M x and implies the eigenvalue route (at the coincident crossing up to their rounding bound); sampled scalar decrease cannot stand in for them.
observation_model: PLSR solve_lyapunov outcome (P or refusal) and verdicts with the returned P and with P = I; SciPy (or the CIW Kronecker solve when SciPy is absent) Lyapunov P per time convention; numpy eigenvalues; PLSR verdicts at 64 sampled states; per scalar-gate sample PLSR's code, max eig(M) and resolution against the exact x^T M x and exact class in rationals; at the coincident crossing also PLSR's x^T M x / |x|^2 less its max eig(M), in units of (gamma_2n n + n^3 u) max|M| read from PLSR's formed M.

title: Compare scalar quadratic and matrix-eigenvalue routes.
uncertainty: Solver differences are at rounding level; route agreement holds only with the stated stability margins. The subnormal scalar entries are reported, not asserted. Which route fires at the coincident crossing is decided by the rounding of the formed M and may differ between BLAS kernels; it is reported, and only its rounding bound is compared.
unresolved_assumptions: Route plants with margins below 0.05 are excluded from the solver and verdict comparisons; near-marginal forms enter only through T107's near-threshold family in the scalar-gate comparison.

At the coincident crossing whether the scalar gate, the eigenvalue route, both or neither fire is decided by the rounding of the formed M and may differ between BLAS kernels; it is retained per sample in routes.json and stated in the numerical result, not compared.

The independent solver is SciPy when installed. Without SciPy the CIW Kronecker solve stands in, but it solves the same Kronecker system with numpy.linalg.solve as PLSR's solve_lyapunov, so agreement with it is then recorded as an ordinary check, not an independent one.
